Studies of the impact of Bad Creek discharge on stratification in Lake Jocassee have been completed and were supplied to the FPC on August 26, 1975. Duke's assessment of the feasibility of using flow augmentation in Howard Creek is continuing as stated.
The analytical study to determine the impact of operation of the Bad Creek Project on stratification in Lake Jocassee has been completed and was also sent to the FPC on August 26, 1975. The analytical model was not applied to Jocassee Station due to the availability of field data.
Duke has supplied the FPC staff with data on the effects of two Jocasses units on stratification. These data show that stratification is disrupted only in the immediate area of the discharge. Since the pumping rate of two Jocasses units (13,000 cfs) is similar to the total discharge rate of Bad Creek (13,200 cfs), it is likely that the effects of Bad Creek discharge on stratification will be very local (also see "Effects of Bad Creek Pumped Storage on Stratification in Lake Jocasses" by Billy L. Edge, supplied to FPC on August 26, 1975). Data on the effects of all four Jocasses units on stratification are presently being analyzed. See Exhibit W, Subsection 3.2.2.2, Amendment 1.
